title: Nouns 2: The Soft Sign and the Tricky Ones
description: The basic ending rule from lesson 1 covers most Russian nouns, but it leaves three small gaps: soft-sign -ь nouns (which can go either way), nouns whose meaning overrides their ending (папа is masculine), and a tiny closed set of -мя neuters (время, имя). This lesson trains all three.
descriptionRussian: Базовое правило окончаний из первого урока охватывает почти все русские существительные, но остаются три маленькие группы: слова на мягкий знак -ь (могут быть как мужского, так и женского рода), слова, у которых значение важнее окончания (папа — мужской), и крошечный закрытый набор средних на -мя (время, имя). Об этих трёх группах и пойдёт речь.
intro: Lesson 1's three endings cover most Russian nouns. This lesson handles the ones that don't play along: words ending in the soft sign, which can be either gender; words that look feminine but name a man; and a tiny neuter set hiding behind an -я. It is a short list, but every word on it is one you will use daily. Close these gaps and the A1 gender system is finished.
rules: Nouns ending in the soft sign -ь can be masculine or feminine; the spelling alone does not pick a gender, so each soft-sign noun is learned together with its gender. Two helpful tendencies: nouns ending in -тель are reliably masculine (учитель, писатель), and nouns ending in -ость are reliably feminine (радость, новость).
Soft-sign nouns to know at A1. Masculine: день, словарь, гость, рубль, январь, февраль. Feminine: ночь, дверь, мать, дочь, тетрадь, площадь, жизнь, осень.

A handful of nouns end in -а or -я but are masculine because the word names a male person: папа, дядя, дедушка, мужчина, юноша. Meaning beats ending here; adjectives and past-tense verbs agree as masculine. «Мой папа пришёл».
A tiny closed set ends in -мя and is neuter. At A1 only two matter: время (time) and имя (name). Agreement is neuter: «моё время», «какое имя?».
Combined with lesson 1, this gives you the full A1 gender system: check the ending first, then check for -ь (recall the word), then check for the male-person and -мя exceptions.
examples: День длинный. (The day is long.) День ends in -ь and is masculine; the adjective длинный agrees as masculine.
Ночь холодная. (The night is cold.) Ночь ends in -ь and is feminine; холодная agrees as feminine.
Учитель пришёл. (The teacher arrived.) The suffix -тель is reliably masculine; the past-tense verb agrees as masculine.
Новость хорошая. (The news is good.) The suffix -ость is reliably feminine; хорошая agrees as feminine.
Мой папа дома. (My dad is home.) Папа ends in -а but is masculine because it names a male person; the possessive мой agrees accordingly.
Это моё время. (This is my time.) Время ends in -я but is part of the special neuter -мя set; the possessive моё agrees as neuter.

tables.title: Soft-Sign Nouns: M vs F (the A1 set to memorise)

items.hint: The soft sign -ь does not pick a gender by itself. You have to know this one.
items.explanation: День is one of the high-frequency soft-sign masculines you memorise individually. Adjectives agree as masculine: тёплый день, мой день.

items.hint: Pair it with день in your head: day vs night, masculine vs feminine.
items.explanation: Ночь is one of the high-frequency soft-sign feminines. The day/night pair (день M / ночь F) is a useful anchor because both end in -ь but split by gender.

items.hint: What suffix does it end in? That suffix is one of the reliable tendencies.
items.explanation: Учитель ends in -тель. The -тель suffix is reliably masculine for agent nouns (учитель, читатель, писатель, родитель). The female-teacher form is the separate word учительница.

items.hint: It ends in -а, which usually means feminine. But what does the word mean?
items.explanation: Папа ends in -а, but it names a male person, and meaning beats ending here. The verb and adjectives agree as masculine: «Мой папа пришёл». The same rule applies to дядя, дедушка, мужчина, юноша.

items.hint: It ends in -я (which usually means feminine), but it belongs to a special small set.
items.explanation: Время is part of the closed -мя set, which is uniformly neuter. The -я ending is a trap; agreement is always neuter: моё время, какое время?, время прошло.

items.hint: What suffix does it end in? That suffix is one of the reliable tendencies.
items.explanation: Новость ends in -ость, the abstract-quality suffix. Every -ость noun is feminine: новость, радость, молодость, грусть, скорость.

patternRecognition.question: Why is учитель masculine, even though it ends in the soft sign -ь?
patternRecognition.explanation: Soft-sign nouns can go either way, but the -тель agent suffix is reliably masculine: учитель, читатель, писатель, родитель. The female-teacher form is a separate word (учительница) built from a different suffix.

patternRecognition.question: Why is дядя masculine, even though it ends in -я?
options: It is part of the -мя neuter set.
It is a meaning override: дядя names a male person.
patternRecognition.answer: It is a meaning override: дядя names a male person.
patternRecognition.explanation: Дядя ends in -я, which usually marks feminine. But meaning beats ending here: words for male people (папа, дядя, дедушка, мужчина, юноша) are masculine. Agreement follows: «мой дядя пришёл», not «моя дядя пришла».

patternRecognition.question: Why is время neuter, even though it ends in -я?
options: It belongs to a small closed set of -мя neuters.
Soft-sign words ending in -я are neuter.
patternRecognition.answer: It belongs to a small closed set of -мя neuters.
patternRecognition.explanation: Время is part of a tiny set of -мя words that are all neuter: время, имя, племя, бремя, знамя, пламя, семя, стремя, темя, вымя. At A1 you only need время and имя; the rest are rare and bookish.

reviewVocab.definition: the soft sign does not signal gender by itself. Each soft-sign noun is learned with its gender. Reliable: -тель → M, -ость → F.
reviewVocab.example: День: M, ночь: F, учитель: M (-тель), радость: F (-ость).

reviewVocab.definition: nouns that name a male person are masculine, even with -а / -я: папа, дядя, дедушка, мужчина, юноша. Agreement follows meaning, not ending.
a tiny set of -мя nouns is neuter despite the -я ending. At A1: время, имя.
reviewVocab.example: Это моё время. Как твоё имя?
